Finding submitted.

**Summary — INDEMN (critical, missing):**

**What we found.** The Agreement has no Licensor indemnity at all. Article XII ("INDEMNITY", p0128–p0129) runs one way only: we indemnify SFG/E-Path FX for anything arising "directly or indirectly" from our exercise of the licence, the conduct of our business, or any breach of any term — and we are additionally made "solely responsible" for all liability flowing from use of the licence.

**Why this is walk-away territory.** Two other clauses compound the exposure:
- Article XIII(a) (p0130): "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY HAS RESULTED ... IN ANY INFRINGEMENT ... OF THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ... RIGHTS OF ANY PERSON," with an aggregate cap of **one half** of fees paid.
- The Article IX warranty disclaimer puts the Licensed Technology on an "AS IS" basis and disclaims non-infringement expressly.

Net effect: we bear 100% of third-party IP infringement risk in software we neither own nor control, while indemnifying the Licensor for our use of it.

**Redline (validated ok:true).**
1. Narrowed our indemnity to third-party claims arising from (i) content/data we provide and (ii) our breach of applicable law; deleted the "solely responsible," "directly or indirectly," and "conduct of Licensee's business" hooks.
2. Inserted new Article XII(b): Licensor defends and indemnifies us and our affiliates for third-party claims of IP infringement/misappropriation by the Licensed Technology, Licensor's breach of law, Licensor-caused unauthorised access to our data, and Licensor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct — with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics.
3. Added an express carve-out from Article XIII, without which the new indemnity would be neutered by the infringement exclusion and half-fees cap.

**Fallback to offer if resisted:** IP-only indemnity with customary modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure–modify–replace–refund remedies, and a 3× annual fees super-cap.
